_comment: Ad density and behaviour, read at runtime by public/ads.js. This file is the committed default; server/index.js serves GET /ads-config.json and merges the ADS_CONFIG environment variable over the top, so densities can be retuned by setting one Fly secret without rebuilding or redeploying the app. See docs/action-plan.md for the tuning procedure and docs/revenue-model.md for what each setting is worth.
_maxSlotsPerPage: Hard ceiling on how many slots fill on one page, counted in document order; the rest are dropped. 0 disables ads without touching markup. The markup sets the intended density (three on content pages); this is the ceiling and the live tuning lever. Set it below the number of slots in the HTML to thin every page at once.
_types: Per-format kill switch. A disabled format never loads and its slot collapses. Use this to pull one unit that is underperforming without editing 282 pages.
_socialBar: Adsterra's dismissible floating Social Bar. It is restricted to editorial/SEO pages and waits for both time-on-page and meaningful scrolling. It never loads in the voice or text app, so a remote creative cannot cover controls or appear during a conversation.
_pauseDuringCall: While a voice call or text chat is live, no slot starts loading, retries a host, or collapses. Ads already on screen stay exactly as they are. This is what keeps a long call free of movement while still earning from impressions placed before it started.
_lazyRootMargin: How far ahead of the viewport a slot begins loading. Larger fills sooner and wastes more impressions on users who never scroll that far; smaller risks an empty slot when the user arrives.
_fillTimeoutMs: How long one serving host is given to put something in the frame before the next host is tried, while the slot is still off screen. Generous on purpose: nobody is looking at it, and a short deadline throws away real fills on slow mobile connections.
_visibleFillTimeoutMs: The same deadline while the slot IS on screen. Much shorter, because every extra second is a second of blank space someone is staring at. An ad blocker or a filtering resolver means the slot will never fill, and this is how fast the page takes that space back.
_fallback: What to put in a slot when the ad network never fills it - most often because the visitor runs an ad blocker or a filtering DNS resolver, which is a large share of this audience. Rather than collapsing to nothing, the slot shows one of our own promos. These are plain first-party HTML with no external request of any kind, so nothing exists for a blocker to block. Never labelled Sponsored, because they are our own content and calling them sponsored would be a lie. Set enabled:false to go back to collapsing.
